summary: Petra Maurer is a Tibetologist and Indologist who studied under Dieter Schuh and Dunchu Sonam Dorje. She held a fellowship at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg in 2017 and posts at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2013) and LMU Munich (attested 2018).

Pham Thi Tuyet Tam works in Buddhist studies. She earned an MA at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under the supervision of Phra Maha Somboon Vuddhikaro and Sanu Mahatthanadull (attested 2017).

Phanit Jetjiravat works in Buddhist studies. Jetjiravat earned a Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, advised by Phra Suthithammanuwat, Veerachart Nimanong, and Paetpong Worapongpichet.

Philip A. Kuhn (1933–2016) was a sinologist and historian who studied at Harvard, SOAS, and Georgetown. He served in the U.S. Armed Forces (1954–1958) and held posts at the University of Chicago (1963–1978) and Harvard, directing the Fairbank Center (1980–1986).

Philip A. Mellor works in religious studies. After completing a doctoral thesis at the University of Manchester in 1989, he served at the University of Leeds as Professor of Religion and Social Theory and Head of the School of Humanities (attested 2010).

Philip B. Yampolsky (1920–1996) specialized in Buddhist studies, sinology, and japanology, studying under Yoshitaka Iriya (~1955–1962). He held teaching and library posts at Columbia University (~1968–1996) and chaired the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (1991–1996).
Philip Deslippe works in religious studies and Indology. He completed a PhD and served as a teaching associate at the University of California, Santa Barbara (attested 2020).

Philip L. Quinn (1940–2004) was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Georgetown, Delaware, and Pittsburgh, and held academic posts at Brown University (~1969–1985) and the University of Notre Dame (~1985–2004).

Philip Whalen (1923–2002) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who studied at Reed College and under Richard Baker (~1972). He served as resident teacher at South Ridge Zendo and abbot of Hartford Street Zen Center (~1991–1996).

Philipp A. Maas works in Indology and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Bonn in 2004 under Claus Vogel and Albrecht Wezler, later holding research posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences, University of Vienna, and Leipzig University (attested 2022).

Philippe Turenne specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned a PhD at McGill University (attested 2010) supervised by G. Victor Sōgen Hori, and studied under Khenpo Palden Sherab, Richard P. Hayes, and several Tibetan traditional teachers.

Philippe-Édouard Foucaux (1811–1894) was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Eugène Burnouf. He was Professor of Tibetan at INALCO (1854) and Professor of Sanskrit at the Collège de France (1857–1894).
Phillip B. Zarrilli (1947–2020) was a scholar in Indology and other fields. He held academic posts at the University of Wisconsin–Madison (~1979–1998) and the University of Exeter (~1998–2020).

Phillip E. Bloom works in sinology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD at Harvard University (attested 2013) under the supervision of Eugene Y. Wang, Yukio Lippit, and James Robson.

Phra Brahmagunabhorn (born 1938) works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University and Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University, later serving as Dean of the Faculty of Buddhist Studies and Deputy Vice Rector at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2012).

Phra Brahmapundit (born 1955) works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He served as Rector of Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (~1997–2018), President of the International Council for the Day of Vesak (~2004), and President of the International Association of Buddhist Universities (~2007).

Phra Kiattisak Ponampon specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He earned an MA at the University of Otago (attested 2015) supervised by Xiaohuan Zhao, Will Sweetman, and Elizabeth Guthrie, and was taught by several scholars in 2013.

Phra Sigambhirayan works in Buddhist studies. He earned a Bachelor of Liberal Arts from Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University and an M.A. in Buddhist Studies from Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.

Phramaha Niras Ruangsan works in Buddhist studies. He completed a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Sydney, supervised by Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle, Peter Oldmeadow, Mark Allon, and Prayong Seanburan.
Phramaha Somboon Watana works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from Panjab University in 1999 under the supervision of Rekha Jhanji and Dharmanand Sharma.
